stage_a.note: The founder maintains a very strong positive and energetic demeanor throughout the entire pitch.
The founder is highly animated, uses frequent gestures, and speaks with pronounced excitement about the service.
The founder displays a very friendly, approachable, and considerate orientation toward the panel.

venture.description: Wedfuly plans and produces remote and hybrid weddings, providing low-tech equipment and remote production to allow guests to attend virtually.
venture.note: The primary industry is wedding services.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: The founder pitches Wedfuly, a service that produces virtual and hybrid weddings, allowing guests to attend remotely.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: The founder invites the panel to eat the cake and drink the champagne provided to them.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Kevin initiates a toast with the champagne.

turns.speaker: PANEL
turns.summary: The panel toasts and cheers together.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Daymond states that he believes weddings should be celebrated in person and exits due to the high valuation.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Kevin jokes that the founder should take Daymond's cake back since he exited.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: The founder laughs and tells Daymond he can still enjoy the cake.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Mark shares a fun fact that the first wedding ever streamed online was his brother's in 1998.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Lori expresses surprise and asks Mark how he knows that.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Mark explains that he started the streaming industry and made his money that way.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: The founder jokingly asks Mark how he knows it was the very first one.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Mark replies that his company did all the streaming at the time.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Robert questions whether people will still want video weddings after the pandemic ends.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: The founder agrees but notes that 40% of their couples chose the service because it fits their specific needs.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Kevin asks how many weddings the company has performed.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: The founder states they have performed 700 weddings since March 2020.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Kevin notes he is heavily involved in the wedding industry and dismisses 700 as a very small number.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: The founder asks to quickly finish her previous point about the 40% statistic.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Daymond interrupts to pause the conversation before discussing money.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Lori asks about the founder's background and how she got into the wedding business.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: The founder explains that her background is actually in software engineering.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Lori acknowledges the founder's background.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: The founder elaborates that she previously worked at a large financial corporation as a software engineer.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Lori comments that she expected it because women can do everything.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: The founder agrees enthusiastically with Lori's statement.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: The founder explains she wanted to move to a female-dominated industry to feel more comfortable, joking about Kevin.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Robert jokes that Kevin doesn't fit in.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: The founder details how she built an app and realized traditional weddings don't fit everyone, leading to her business model.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Robert asks how the service works step-by-step after a customer signs up.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: The founder explains the process, from a preparation guide to the remote, low-tech, multimedia production on the wedding day.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Kevin asks how many weddings the company can handle on a single Saturday.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: The founder replies they handled 30 weddings on one Saturday and highlights their scalable operations.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Mark asks what proprietary technology or production switching tools the founder actually developed.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: The founder clarifies that the proprietary technology lies in the planning process and data collection guide flow.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Mark asks if the company is also a data business and what specific information they are aggregating.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: The founder confirms they aggregate detailed data about each wedding, including the guest list.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Kevin asks specifically if they capture birth dates or other detailed information about the attendees.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: The founder says they currently collect the first name, last name, and email of attendees.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Daymond brings the focus back to valuation, asking for the sales from the last year and year-to-date.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: The founder states they have done a million dollars in sales since March 2020.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Robert expresses positive surprise at the sales figure.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Kevin asks if the business was profitable on that million dollars in sales.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: The founder confirms profitability, detailing revenue and profit for the previous and current years.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Lori asks for the average revenue per customer.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: The founder states the average is $1500, explaining the base packages and add-on menu.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Kevin asks for the profit margin on the average $1500 revenue.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: The founder concisely states the profit margin is 75%.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Robert asks if the founder has raised any outside money.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: The founder confirms she has not raised money and owns 100% of the company.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Mark commends the founder for owning the entire company.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Kevin makes an offer, leveraging his other wedding businesses to create a feeder system and asking for more equity.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: The founder thanks Kevin and counters his offer, asking for the same amount but less equity.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Kevin declines the counter-offer, reiterating the value he brings and keeping his original offer firm.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Lori praises the founder's story but states the business is not right for her and exits.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: The founder thanks Lori for her kind words.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Mark expresses concerns about the business's scalability and his lack of ancillary businesses, and exits.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: The founder thanks Mark for his feedback.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Robert praises the founder and offers to accept the exact counter-offer she had proposed to Kevin.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: After a brief pause, the founder accepts Robert's offer.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Robert enthusiastically celebrates the deal.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Daymond jokes that Robert snatched the deal right away from Kevin.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Robert and the founder celebrate by popping confetti poppers.

decisions.note: He believes weddings should be in person and does not like the valuation.
Wants to use the business as a feeder for his other wedding-related companies.
Thanks him for the offer but asks to lower the equity.
Declines the counter, stating he brings too much value to lower the equity.
Loves the founder's story but feels the business is not right for her.
Has concerns about scalability and lacks ancillary businesses to support it.
Believes the founder is a great operator and accepts her counter-offer terms.
Accepts Robert's offer after Kevin remains silent.

record.notes: The founder and Robert pop confetti at the end to celebrate the deal.
